items.title: October 21st, 2026
items.text:
Enhancement: Start Browser Discovery from Managed Devices or Third-Party MDM
Feature: AI & SaaS Management
Browser discovery in AI & SaaS Management can now start when a user signs in to a JumpCloud-managed device associated with them, or when you deploy the JumpCloud Go extension through a third-party MDM provider.
Use the path that matches how you manage devices and identity:
JumpCloud-managed devices: Tracking can start after a user signs in to a JumpCloud-managed device associated with them.
Third-party MDM: Copy the Client ID and Client secret from Settings, add them to the JumpCloud Go extension distribution policy, and deploy that policy. Discovery can start after the extension is installed. Discovery data is associated with a user after they sign in to the User Portal or a JumpCloud SSO application, or after they sign in to a JumpCloud-managed device associated with them.
See Get Started: AI & SaaS Management and Deploy JumpCloud Go Extension for SaaS Discovery with Third-Party MDM to learn more.

items.title: October 16, 2026
items.text:
Enhancement: App Catalog Update Experience Enhancements
Feature: Software Management
Control App Catalog update notifications and let users start available updates from the Self Service App Catalog.
Update notification control: Select Disable end user update notifications when adding or editing an application. This setting applies to Auto and Self Service delivery. Existing applications keep notifications enabled. With Auto-Update enabled, updates are still forced after seven days, even when notifications are off.
Required app updates: Users can start available updates for Required applications from Updates in the Self Service App Catalog. Required applications remain visible regardless of the Auto-Update setting.
See Use the JumpCloud App Catalog for macOS, Use the JumpCloud App Catalog for Windows, and Get Started: Self Service App Catalog to learn more.

items.title: October 14th, 2026
items.text:
New: Agent Uninstall Protection
Feature: Device Management
Prevent unauthorized removal of the JumpCloud agent so your devices stay managed. Agent Uninstall Protection is on by default for all devices running JumpCloud agent v2.179.2 or later. Uninstalling the agent with standard methods on macOS, Windows, and Linux now requires a per-device maintenance token.
Directory Insights Events: Directory Insights logs failed uninstall attempts, successful uninstalls, and exemption policy changes, identifying the device and the user.
Maintenance Tokens: Admins with Manager role permissions or higher can view a device's maintenance token from the device details. Tokens work without network connectivity and automatically rotate 60 minutes after they're viewed if the agent remains installed.
Exemption Policies: Use the Disable Agent Uninstall Protection policy for macOS, Windows, or Linux to remove the token requirement from specific devices during agent maintenance, troubleshooting, or imaging.
Protection Status: View each device's protection status (On, Off, or Failed) from the device details or the Devices list.
Deleting an active device from the Admin Portal or the JumpCloud API still removes the agent without a maintenance token.
Available in the Admin Portal: Go to Device Management > Devices > Settings > Agent Uninstall Protection.
Learn More
Get Started: Agent Uninstall Protection
Create a Device Level macOS Disable Agent Uninstall Protection Policy
Create a Device Level Windows Disable Agent Uninstall Protection Policy
Create a Device Level Linux Disable Agent Uninstall Protection Policy
Install or Uninstall the JumpCloud Agent
Enhancement: Customize Email and Automation Variables tabs in Settings
Feature: Admin Portal
You'll see a refreshed look on the Customize Email and Automation Variables tabs, with shorter labels and helper text that's easier to scan. Your settings work exactly as before. They're just easier to find and update.
See Settings in the Admin Portal to learn more.

items.title: October 13th, 2026
items.text:
Enhancement: AI Agent Management APIs
Feature: Agent Identities
JumpCloud now provides REST APIs for managing AI Agents and Agent Groups, enabling administrators and developers to automate agent identity management and integrate it into existing workflows.
With these APIs, you can:
Manage AI Agents: Register, retrieve, update, suspend, activate, and delete agent identities programmatically.
Manage Agent Credentials: Create, retrieve, update, and delete credentials associated with AI Agents.
Manage Agent Groups: Create, update, and delete groups to organize agents and simplify access management.
Manage Group Memberships and Application Assignments: Add or remove agents from groups, manage group application assignments, and retrieve applications assigned to individual agents.
For more information, see the API documentation:
Agents API
Agent Groups API
New: Custom Messaging
Feature: User Portal
Create login dialogs and announcement banners for users in the User Portal. Choose who sees each message by user group, set the severity or message type so the right alerts stand out, and publish when you’re ready.
Available in the Admin Portal: Go to Settings > User Portal > Custom Messaging.
See Get Started: Custom Messaging to learn more.

items.title: September 30th, 2026
items.text:
Enhancement: Automatic registration for JumpCloud Go
Feature: JumpCloud Go
JumpCloud Go™ automatic device registration is now available. Managed Windows, macOS, and Linux devices bound to a user automatically register for JumpCloud Go after user sign-in, removing the need for manual browser registration prompts. Admins can control device eligibility using device exclusion groups and fall back to manual registration if automatic registration fails.
See Use JumpCloud Go™ to learn more.
New: Custom Banned Password List
Feature: Password Policies
JumpCloud now supports a Custom Banned Password List, allowing organization administrators to block specific words, terms, and phrases from being used in user passwords.
See Custom Banned Password List to learn more.
New: User Portal Folders
Feature: User Portal
Let end users organize assigned applications into personal folders on the All Applications page. Users can create folders and add applications from the Folders tab. They can also add an application to a folder from its card on All Applications.
Folders are private to each user. Other users and IT admins cannot see or manage another user’s folders, and applications stay available on All Applications.
Available in the User Portal: Go to All Applications > Folders.
Learn More
Get Started: User Portal Folders
Get Started: User Portal
New: App Settings Privacy Policies for Apple MDM
Feature: Policy Management
JumpCloud now supports App Settings Privacy policies for Apple MDM. Recommend privacy permission defaults for one or more applications so that when a matching app launches, users see a consent prompt with your organization justification and can allow those defaults or continue with the standard prompts.
New Apple Policies
User Level macOS App Settings Privacy — Recommend privacy permission defaults for matching applications on supervised Mac computers running macOS 27 or later. Assign the policy to users or user groups. Supported permissions include Accessibility, Bluetooth, Camera, Dictation, Local network, Location, and Microphone.
Device Level iOS and iPadOS App Settings Privacy — Recommend privacy permission defaults for matching applications on supervised iPhone and iPad devices running iOS 27 or later or iPadOS 27 or later. Assign the policy to devices or device groups. Supported permissions include Bluetooth, Camera, Dictation, Local Network, Location, Location Accuracy, and Microphone.
See Create a User Level macOS App Settings Privacy Policy and Create a Device Level iOS and iPadOS App Settings Privacy Policy to learn more.
New: User Portal Asset Visibility and Acknowledgement
Feature: Asset Management
Give end users visibility into assets assigned to them in the User Portal, and let admins request acknowledgement from the asset owner when an asset is assigned or reassigned. Each request and response is recorded in Asset History, and email notifications keep admins and users informed.
Enable the feature: Go to Device Management > Asset Management > Settings and Fields > General Settings. In the User Portal section, enable Asset Visibility and Asset Acknowledgement.
Learn More
Get Started: Asset Management
Configure Asset Management
Get Started: User Portal
New: JumpCloud MCP Server for Users
Feature: JumpCloud MCP Server for Users
The Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server for Users enables JumpCloud users to connect their preferred AI clients directly to supported User Portal capabilities using OAuth sessions. This allows users to perform routine tasks without leaving their AI tools.
Admin Controls: Go to Settings > JumpCloud AI and toggle on MCP Server for Users to enable the feature. You can review active client sessions and revoke them manually, or configure an automatic expiration window.
User Visibility: Users can view and revoke their own active sessions by going to Security > JumpCloud MCP in the User Portal.
See Get Started: JumpCloud MCP Server for Users to learn more.
New: Custom Risk Policies
Feature: Access Risk
Tailor risk detection for Admin Portal, User Portal, device, and SSO application logins. Create policies for specific user groups or SSO applications, choose which risk factors to monitor, and adjust their score contributions. Set policy precedence when multiple policies apply; the Default Policy provides coverage for logins outside your custom policies.
See Configure Custom Risk Policies to learn more.

items.title: September 29th, 2026
items.text:
New: Android Policy Expansion
Feature: Policy Management
JumpCloud has expanded Android policy management with new policies for display, autofill, work account authentication, and default app handling, plus enhanced Bluetooth controls. These policies help you enforce security and productivity settings on managed Android devices enrolled in JumpCloud EMM.
New Android Policies
Display Settings — Control screen brightness and screen timeout. Choose whether end users configure display settings themselves, or enforce fixed brightness and timeout values on supported devices.
Autofill — Control system autofill for forms in apps and websites. Allow users to choose an autofill service, or disable autofill and lock the setting on Android 8.0 and later.
Work Account — Configure whether device management requires a Google authenticated enterprise account, and optionally require a specific Google Account email during setup.
Default App and Intent Handling — Set an approved managed app as the default handler for selected Android activities, such as opening web links or dialing phone numbers, so Android opens the configured app instead of the app chooser.
Enhanced Android Policy
Bluetooth Restrictions — In addition to disabling Bluetooth, blocking Bluetooth configuration, and preventing work contact sharing, you can now control outbound Bluetooth file sharing. On company-owned devices with a work profile, you can also restrict Bluetooth sharing on the personal profile through the Work & Personal Usage policy.
See Configure Settings for Android Policies to learn more.

items.title: September 25th, 2026
items.text:
Enhancement: Dormant Application Access Detection
Feature: Access Risk
Dormant Application Access now detects when a user signs back into an SSO application after a period of inactivity that meets your configured threshold, instead of flagging first-time access. You can set the dormant application threshold in Access Risk > Configuration. First-time access to an application does not trigger this factor, which reduces noise from newly provisioned apps.
See Configure Access Risk Detection to learn more.

items.title: September 24th, 2026
items.text:
New: Patch Management Dashboards
Feature: Patch Management
JumpCloud Patch Management now includes a unified dashboard experience plus dedicated Windows and Apple views in the Admin Portal. From Device Management > Patch Management, you can monitor fleet-wide update posture, drill into KB compliance on Windows devices, and track Apple OS rollout progress against active update policies.
Unified Patch Dashboard
Cross-platform overview: Review patch compliance for Windows and Apple devices together on the Overview tab.
Fleet update summary: See pending updates by severity, devices with pending updates, devices with update failures, and the age of missing updates.
Platform switcher: Move between Overview, Apple, and Windows tabs from one page.
Windows Overview and Patch List
Patch and device insights: View patch coverage, missing patches by severity and age, device compliance, and critical patch exposure in one dashboard.
Global severity filter: Focus the dashboard and KB list on the severities that matter most.
KB-centric control: Search and filter KBs, review CVE details, approve awaiting updates, retry failed installations, and export the KB list as CSV or JSON.
Bulk remediation: Install missing critical patches or non-compliant device updates immediately or on the policy schedule.
Apple Compliance Dashboard
Rollout visibility: Track OS deployment progress for macOS, iOS, and iPadOS devices against effective update policy targets.
Compliance and coverage: Review missing updates by severity, device compliance, update policy coverage, and the age of missing updates.
Apple OS Version Listing: Filter by platform, release date, severity, and device status; drill into targeted, installed, pending, in-progress, or failed devices; and view associated CVE details.
Learn More

items.title: September 21st, 2026
items.text:
New: Device Patch Report (Windows)
Feature: JumpCloud Reports
The Device Patch Report (Windows) gives IT admins per-device visibility into Windows Knowledge Base (KB) patch installation status in the JumpCloud Admin Portal. The report is auto-populated from existing patch data.
Per-device KB status: View Installed, Pending, and Failed status for each KB on each managed Windows device.
Preview and export: Preview up to 500 rows in the Admin Portal, or download the complete organization result set as CSV.
No manual setup: Report data syncs from existing Windows patch inventory.
See Device Patch Report to learn more.

items.title: September 18th, 2026
items.text:
Enhancement: Update Existing Application Versions in the Private Repository
Feature: Software Management
You can now update the binary of an existing custom application in JumpCloud's Private Repository instead of creating a new application for every release. Upload the new file from Update Version on the application's Details tab, and JumpCloud deploys it to devices already associated with the application.
Consistent update process: Use the same Upload File flow for new applications and version updates, on both Windows and Apple applications.
Fewer manual steps: Skip re-creating the application, reassigning devices, and rebinding device groups for each new version.
Windows EXE updates: Enter an install success exit code before you deploy an EXE update, so JumpCloud can confirm the installation succeeded.
See Manage Software with the JumpCloud Private Repository to learn more.

items.title: September 16th, 2026
items.text:
New: Knowledge Base Uploads for AI Assistant
Feature: AI Assistant
You can now upload internal documentation directly into a private, org-scoped knowledge base for AI Assistant. The assistant references your uploaded content to answer questions about organization-specific processes, runbooks, SOPs, and policies. Supported formats include PDF, TXT, DOCX, and MD (10 MB maximum per file, 25 files maximum per org). When a response uses your uploaded documentation, AI Assistant clearly attributes the source document in the chat.
See Get Started: JumpCloud AI Admin Assistant to learn more.
Enhancement: AI Gateway Dashboard
Feature: AI Gateway
The AI Gateway now includes a Dashboard tab with org-wide visibility into MCP server usage, tool call volume, and error rates. Summary cards, trend charts, and rankings for top servers, clients, and users help you monitor adoption and investigate failures. Click an MCP server to drill into server-specific metrics.
See Get Started: AI Gateway to learn more.
Enhancement: Agent Client Authentication Type
Feature: Agent Identities
You can now configure the client authentication type for an agent's OAuth credentials. On the agent's Authentication tab, choose how the agent platform sends the client ID and secret when requesting a token from JumpCloud:
Client secret basic: Sends credentials in the authorization header. This is the default option.
Client secret post: Sends credentials in the request body.
This ensures you can match the exact authentication method required by your external platform's OAuth configuration, such as Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.
See Get Started: Agents to learn more.

items.title: September 14th, 2026
items.text:
New: Block macOS Golden Gate Installer Policy
Feature: Policy Management
Use the Block macOS Golden Gate Installer policy to prevent the macOS 27 Golden Gate installer from launching on MDM-enrolled Mac computers. If users download the installer from the App Store or another source, the installer is automatically terminated when they try to launch it. To also keep macOS 27 Golden Gate from appearing in Software Update, defer major OS upgrades in your Patch Management policies for up to 90 days.
Available in the Admin Portal: Go to Device Management > Policy Management, click + Add New > Device Policy, and select the macOS tab.
See Create a Mac Policy to Delay or Block Golden Gate to learn more.
